Ausleihen or Verleihen? German B1 Word-Choice Practice

Practise sich etwas ausleihen for borrowing and verleihen for lending or awarding. Learn German usage overlap with translated examples and explained answers.

B1 level4 worked examples4 practice questions

Independent practice by Klarweg. Not an official Goethe exam or assessment.

Understand the difference

Sich etwas ausleihen commonly means borrowing something temporarily. Jemandem etwas verleihen means lending something; verleihen also means awarding a prize or title. Ausleihen without a reflexive pronoun can likewise mean lending, so the two verbs are not opposites in every construction.

Common mistake to avoid

Ich leihe dir mein Fahrrad aus is a valid lending sentence. For unambiguous borrowing in these tasks, use the reflexive pattern mir etwas ausleihen.

How to practise: read the examples once, cover the English meanings and try explaining the choice aloud. Next, complete all four questions before opening their answers.

Four German examples with English meanings

Pay attention to the exact article, verb position or ending described in the rule.

Worked example 1Ich leihe mir eine Kamera für den Ausflug aus.I borrow a camera for the outing.
Worked example 2Die Stadt verleiht ihr einen Kulturpreis.The city awards her a cultural prize.
Worked example 3Der Verein verleiht Sportgeräte an seine Mitglieder.The association lends sports equipment to its members.
Worked example 4Wir leihen uns in der Bibliothek einen Film aus.We borrow a film from the library.

Practice: choose the right word

Choose ausleihen for the supplied reflexive borrowing pattern or verleihen for the specified award. The usage note also explains overlap in lending. Try each question before opening the answer. A dash (—) means no word is needed. Where another answer is possible, the explanation notes it. These are self-check exercises, not exam scoring.

Question 1. Ich möchte mir für das Wochenende ein Zelt ___. (borrow)

Show answer and explanation for question 1

Answer: ausleihen

Mir ein Zelt ausleihen is the reflexive borrowing pattern.

Question 2. Die Jury wird morgen den Preis ___. (award)

Show answer and explanation for question 2

Answer: verleihen

Einen Preis verleihen means awarding a prize, not borrowing it.

Question 3. Wir möchten uns zwei Fahrräder ___. (borrow)

Show answer and explanation for question 3

Answer: ausleihen

Uns marks the borrowers in sich Fahrräder ausleihen.

Question 4. Die Universität wird ihr einen Ehrentitel ___. (award a title)

Show answer and explanation for question 4

Answer: verleihen

Einen Ehrentitel verleihen is the established award expression.
